timeline.title: Founding of India's Space Programme
timeline.description: India's space effort began under Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, starting with sounding rocket launches from Thumba and culminating in the establishment of ISRO in 1969.

timeline.title: Aryabhata — India's First Satellite
timeline.description: India's first satellite, named after the ancient astronomer, was launched with Soviet assistance, marking the country's entry into space.

timeline.title: PSLV — Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle
timeline.description: ISRO's workhorse launch vehicle, renowned for its reliability, used for Earth observation, navigation, and interplanetary missions including Chandrayaan-1 and Mangalyaan.

timeline.title: GSLV — Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle
timeline.description: Developed to launch heavier payloads into geostationary transfer orbit, including India's own cryogenic upper stage technology.

timeline.title: Chandrayaan-1
timeline.description: India's first lunar mission, which helped confirm the presence of water molecules on the Moon's surface.

timeline.title: Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission)
timeline.description: India's first interplanetary mission, making ISRO one of the first space agencies to reach Mars orbit on its first attempt.

timeline.title: LVM3 (formerly GSLV Mk III)
timeline.description: ISRO's most powerful launch vehicle, capable of carrying heavier payloads to orbit and crewed spacecraft for the Gaganyaan programme.

timeline.title: Chandrayaan-2
timeline.description: An orbiter, lander, and rover mission to the Moon; the orbiter continues to return valuable science data.

timeline.title: Chandrayaan-3
timeline.description: Successfully landed near the Moon's south polar region, making India one of a small number of nations to achieve a soft lunar landing.

timeline.title: Aditya-L1
timeline.description: India's first dedicated solar observation mission, positioned near the Sun-Earth L1 Lagrange point to study the Sun continuously.

timeline.title: SSLV — Small Satellite Launch Vehicle
timeline.description: A smaller, faster-turnaround launch vehicle designed for the growing small-satellite market.

timeline.title: Gaganyaan — Human Spaceflight Programme
timeline.description: India's programme to independently launch astronauts into low Earth orbit, including uncrewed test flights ahead of a crewed mission.

timeline.title: Future Exploration
timeline.description: ISRO has publicly discussed further lunar missions, a planned Indian space station, and continued interplanetary ambitions. See the official ISRO website for current programme status.
